requirements.statement: The live animals notification list is the page at the live-animals set root in the animals frontend, and it reads the animals backend's notification list.
requirements.why: The afternoon rulings of 9 October keep each notification list in its own frontend and reframe it in place, built on the animals frontend and animals backend; this replaces, for this programme, the move to the INS frontend that the morning ruling had kept from Rhys's DR1 judgement (c-159).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-001 (proven by trace-e2e-p3-001 and repo-tests-p3-067): the list is already the animals frontend's page at the live-animals set root, and it reads the animals backend's list (repo-frontend-p4-024, repo-perftests-p2-042); what the page shows changes under the requirements that follow.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's browser title is 'Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK', with the caption 'Dashboard' above an h1 naming the category, 'Live animals'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles every list 'Dashboard' and heads it with the category, so a trader can tell which category's notifications they are looking at; the 9 October afternoon ruling names this frame for the reframed list. Plants' own list takes the same title in the same increment (req-2028).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page title and the h1 are both 'Import notification service' (repo-frontend-p4-004), so the browser title reads 'Import notification service - Import notification service - GOV.UK'; the 'Dashboard' caption already exists (repo-frontend-p4-003).

requirements.statement: On the live animals, germinal products and plants lists the heading is followed straight away by the 'Create new' button, with no introductory paragraph, no guidance sentence and no Messages link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's category list goes straight from its heading to its actions; plants takes the same frame in the same increment (9 October afternoon ruling, claim 55).
requirements.deltaNote: Today one paragraph about telling the authorities about imported live animals sits under the animals heading, and plants' list has its own intro paragraph about high-risk plants (its guidance-link sentence renders only when a guidance address is supplied, and none is). The 'Use template' button Design Release 2.1 puts beside 'Create new' is not built while templates are parked (req-1038).

requirements.statement: The list page has a 'Back' link to the overall home.
requirements.why: Not built: the 9 October afternoon ruling sends every page Design Release 2.1 points at the overall dashboard to the set's own list, and has the INS front door reached through the service navigation as today, so the list, now the set's own landing page, carries no Back link (c-298).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has a primary 'Create new' button, which starts a live animals notification and carries the list's category into the create journey. Where it points and how the category is carried are the services' to name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 starts a notification from 'Create new', carrying the category the trader was looking at; the 9 October rulings keep the destination and the category, not the prototype's create-notification?category= address (c-251), and name 'Create new' starting a notification as part of the reframed list's frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a GOV.UK start button 'Start a new notification' posts to the set's notifications path, which creates a draft and its reference on every press and redirects straight to its origin page (repo-frontend-p4-007, p4-008).

requirements.statement: The live animals and germinal products lists have a secondary 'Use template' button beside 'Create new' that goes to the templates page.
requirements.why: Not built: Design Release 2.1 offers starting from a saved template on every category list, but templates are parked and dropped for now, so the lists offer no way into them (c-420), and the button is built only when templates are planned again. Plants was never in scope for templates.

requirements.statement: The list page has an h2 'Summary' section with two glance cards: 'Action needed' with 'Tasks requiring your attention' and a 'View tasks' link to the action-needed page filtered to the category, and 'Status updated' with 'Changes in the past 24 hours' and a 'View updates' link to the changes page filtered to the category.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts what needs the trader's attention at the top of each category list; the 9 October afternoon ruling counts the list's Summary cards (inc-139) as the INS dashboard's summary information, blocked until its requirements firm up.
requirements.blockedBy: The INS dashboard's requirements firm up (Sam, 9 October): the counts, glance cards and drill-downs are summary information, re-distilled once those requirements exist.

requirements.statement: The list's 'Action needed' glance card shows a live count for the category of the notifications that need something from the trader, matching the Action needed list its link opens.
requirements.why: The count is only useful if it agrees with the drill-down page. It is summary information, blocked with the Summary cards, and what counts as needing action now waits on the outstanding-actions banner the dashboard designs under test introduce (16 November ruling).
requirements.blockedBy: The INS dashboard's requirements firm up (Sam, 9 October) and the outstanding-actions banner the dashboard designs under test introduce is agreed (Sam, 16 November), because nothing action-required is shown until then.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list the notifications sit under an h2 'Notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads the list section 'Notifications'; DR1's 'My notifications' row was only deferred, never judged; plants takes the same frame. DR1's inc-021 also left open whether the breadcrumb label that shares these words on the delete and cancel-amendment pages follows the heading, which those pages' own area settles.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both lists use the medium h2 'Your notifications' (Welsh 'Eich hysbysiadau'), which the animals frontend also uses as the breadcrumb label on the delete and cancel-amendment pages.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list the search and sort sit in one column above the cards inside the 'Notifications' section, with no 'Filter notifications' heading and no separate one-third filter aside beside the results; on the live animals list the 'Additional filters' disclosure follows them, above the tabs.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lays the list out as one column: search and sort, then the filters disclosure, then the tabs and cards. Plants takes the same frame in the same increment, its filters aside (9 October afternoon ruling).
requirements.deltaNote: Today both lists are two columns inside the full-width content column: a one-third aside headed 'Filter notifications' (h3) holding the search, and a two-thirds column holding the results count, sort and cards (repo-frontend-p4-013, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-054).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's search field is labelled 'Search by'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label; today's 'Keyword or reference' promises a keyword search the service does not give.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the field is labelled 'Keyword or reference' (small bold label) and named referenceNumber.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's search field has the hint 'Keyword, notification number, commodity, consignee or consignor'.
requirements.why: The hint tells the trader what the search matches.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's search is submitted by a real submit button that shows only a magnifying-glass icon and whose accessible name is 'Search'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search control; the 9 October afternoon ruling lets the icon-only button stand as long as it is a real submit button of the GET form (c-299).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the button is a standard primary GOV.UK button with the visible text 'Search'.

requirements.statement: A search on the live animals list lists the notifications whose reference number, commodity, consignee or consignor contains the searched text, ignoring case.
requirements.why: The hint promises a keyword search over those facts, and DR1's own inc-019 row read the same three things as searchable. The prototype cannot persist or query, so its search is inert; a real search box that does nothing would mislead the trader, so the real service applies it (c-162).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the term is passed to the listing only as referenceNumber, an exact match on a complete reference, so a commodity or a party name finds nothing (repo-frontend-p4-016, repo-tests-p3-089).

requirements.statement: After a search the field keeps the searched text, and searching with an empty or whitespace-only field clears the search and lists everything again.
requirements.why: The trader can see and change what they searched for; both Design Release 2.1 and today keep the text.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-017, p4-022 and p4-023: the field is filled with the current term, and a blank or whitespace-only term means no filter.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list, search, sort and every additional filter are one GET form to the list's own path, submitted by the search button or by the 'Apply filters' button; it carries the current tab (unless it is the default tab) and the current page (when above 1) as hidden fields, so the result stays on that tab. Changing a select or a radio submits nothing by itself.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts sort and filters inside the search form, and both its search button and its 'Apply filters' button submit that one form; the 9 October afternoon ruling makes it one GET form whose submit buttons search, sort and filter on the server, so the page works without JavaScript. Today search and sort are two forms and a search always restarts at page 1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the search form carries only the sort as a hidden field (no page, no tab), and the sort is a separate GET form (repo-frontend-p4-018, p4-036).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's sort select is labelled 'Sort by:'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the sort control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the select is labelled 'Sort by' with no colon (small bold label).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's sort select offers exactly 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', in that order, with no unselected 'Select one' option.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the sort three orderings; DR1 already rejected an unsorted 'Select one' state, so the list is always sorted, and its own sort-label row was deferred while the list was thought temporary, never judged (c-167).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the options are 'Arrival (newest to oldest)', 'Arrival (oldest to newest)', 'Date created (newest to oldest)' and 'Date created (oldest to newest)'.

requirements.statement: The live animals list is always sorted and the sort is applied for real: 'Newest first' and 'Oldest first' order by when the notification was created, 'Arrival date' orders by arrival date newest first, and with no sort chosen the list is ordered by arrival date newest first with 'Arrival date' selected.
requirements.why: DR1 judged the list always sorted; the prototype never orders its list, so the real service applies the orderings, keeping today's default order (which the prototype's completed tab also shows).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the default is 'Arrival (newest to oldest)' and any unknown value falls back to it; no end-to-end test proves the order of the cards (repo-tests-p3-098).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has no 'Update sort' button: the chosen sort is applied by the search button, or by 'Apply filters', with the rest of the form, and the chosen option stays selected after the page reloads.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's sort has no button of its own; DR1 only deferred this difference, and the 9 October afternoon ruling has one submit button for the whole form, with no select submitting on change.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a separate GET sort form with a secondary 'Update sort' button applies the sort, carrying the page and the search as hidden fields (repo-frontend-p4-029, p4-034).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has an 'Additional filters' disclosure built from the GOV.UK details component inside the search form, closed on load and open whenever an arrival-date, date-range or status filter is set, so after applying a filter the trader sees the filters they chose.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the extra filters out of the way until the trader needs them; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the disclosure from GOV.UK details rather than the prototype's custom chevron markup (c-299).

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'By arrival date' column of small GOV.UK radios 'Today', 'Tomorrow' and 'Next 7 days' (legend visually hidden, the same words shown as its heading); choosing one and searching lists only notifications arriving in that range, and the choice stays checked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader find what is arriving soon; the prototype's filter is inert, so the real service applies it.

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'By date range' column with the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026' and two MoJ date pickers, 'Start date' and 'End date' (a 'Choose date' calendar opening on the current month, weeks starting Monday, each a plain text field without JavaScript); the list shows only notifications arriving between the two dates, and the entered dates are kept.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's date range. DR1's own row records that the design never says which date a date filter narrows, so three things settle it on the arrival date: the radios beside it name the arrival date in their legend and heading, DR1's row has those radios built on this same range rather than on parameters of their own, and the arrival date is the only date Design Release 2.1's card shows at all. The 9 October afternoon ruling accepts the MoJ date picker here, because the range is a search filter, not a date read from a document, and the interaction designer keeps that picker as the one every other date in both frontends uses.

requirements.statement: When the start or end date cannot be read as a date, or the end date is before the start date, the list shows a GOV.UK error summary and an inline error on the date field ('Enter a real start date', 'Enter a real end date' or 'End date must be the same as or after the start date'), opens 'Additional filters', keeps the entered text in the 'Start date' and 'End date' pickers, and lists notifications without the date-range filter.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so a date the filter cannot use is answered with an error rather than silently ignored; the prototype still sets the labels and keeps the entered dates, and the GOV.UK date-input error pattern supplies the messages (c-166, which the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps). The 26 October ruling sets the same shape for any answer that is missing or not valid: an error message for each one, the trader kept on the page, and what they typed never dropped.

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'Status' select offering 'All statuses' (the default, meaning no status filter), 'Draft', 'Amend', 'Submitted' and 'Past'; choosing one and applying the filters lists only drafts not being amended, notifications being amended, submitted notifications or completed notifications respectively, and the choice stays selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's status filter offers each stage a notification can be at, using the same words as its tabs and status tags. 'Past' matches nothing until a real source of completion exists (16 November ruling), and the select still offers it because the design names it. Which words the tabs and this filter use is the tab vocabulary question (c-notification-list-003).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has three tabs, 'Submitted', 'Draft and Amend' and 'Past', built as MoJ sub navigation, each a link that loads the page with that tab chosen; 'Submitted' is the list with no tab chosen, an unknown or missing tab shows 'Submitted', and following a tab drops the search, sort and filters. The tab parameter's name and values are the animals frontend's.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 separates submitted notifications, unfinished work and finished notifications, and drafts keep a home on the list, which DR1 said must not be lost; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the tabs as MoJ sub navigation on the animals frontend's own list, and the prototype never names query parameters (c-251). The 9 October afternoon ruling named the then prototype's tabs 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed', while the 26 November prototype names them 'Submitted', 'Draft and Amend' and 'Past'; which words are built is an open question whose default is the 26 November prototype's (c-notification-list-003).

requirements.statement: The 'Submitted' tab lists submitted notifications, the 'Draft and Amend' tab lists drafts and notifications being amended, and the 'Past' tab lists completed notifications.
requirements.why: Each tab holds the notifications at that stage, as Design Release 2.1 sets them out; a notification submitted with something outstanding is submitted like any other (16 November ruling), and a notification being amended sits with the drafts, as the design groups them (c-165).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended is listed in the 'Draft and Amend' tab with a yellow 'Amend' tag and its status-driven actions (Resume, 'Copy as new', 'Cancel amendment' and Delete).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives a notification being amended its own yellow 'Amend' tag and groups it with the drafts under 'Draft and Amend'; listing it there is how the page reads, which the backend's AMEND lifecycle does not stop (c-165). DR1's judgement keeps its status-driven actions (c-160).
requirements.deltaNote: Today an amending notification is listed with every other notification and there are no tabs; its tag already reads 'Amend' in yellow from the shared status kit (repo-frontend-p4-085).

requirements.statement: The 'Submitted' and 'Draft and Amend' tabs each show their count in bold brackets, such as 'Submitted (2)' and 'Draft and Amend (3)'; 'Past' shows none, even when selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts the notifications still in play; the counts belong to the tabs, which the 9 October afternoon ruling builds now, not to the blocked Summary cards.

requirements.statement: Under the tabs the cards sit under an h3 naming the tab: 'Submitted notifications', 'Draft notifications' or 'Past notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's subheading for each tab panel.

requirements.statement: The live animals list shows 8 notifications a page.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling pages the reframed list 8 at a time, which is also Design Release 2.1's page size for every list and the figure the rest of the estate pages at; how many rows a page holds over a dataset that grows is not the prototype's to set (23 November ruling), so the ruling is the authority and the prototype agrees with it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page size comes from the listing: 25 from the animals backend (end to end) and 20 from the frontend stub (fit), and the page reports the size it is given (repo-frontend-p4-070).

requirements.statement: A list of more than one page shows GOV.UK pagination with numbered page links, a 'Previous' link from page 2 and a 'Next' link before the last page; a list of one page, or no results, shows no pagination. This holds on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses numbered pagination; today both lists have only Previous and Next. Pagination is kept and wanted wherever a list is paged (25 November ruling), and plants takes the same paging in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both lists use block-style pagination with only Previous and Next links and no page numbers, reading 'Next' and 'Previous' rather than the 'Next page' and 'Previous page' the suite's other lists use (repo-tests-p3-082).

requirements.statement: A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and a page past the last shows the last page, on the live animals list as on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 clamps the page, so a stale or hand-typed page never shows an empty list; plants' list already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-075, p4-076 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-033: both lists already ignore a page that is not a whole number of at least one and clamp a page past the last to the last page.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's page links keep the tab (unless 'In progress'), the sort (unless the default), the search text and every additional filter.
requirements.why: Because the real search and filters apply, a page link that dropped them would show a different, unfiltered list on page 2 (c-163).
requirements.deltaNote: Today Previous and Next keep the sort (unless the default) and the reference search, and the list's address carries only what differs from the default view; there are no tabs or filters to keep (repo-frontend-p4-035, p4-074).

requirements.statement: Neither the live animals list nor plants' list shows a 'Showing ... results' count above the cards, on any tab or page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's category list works out a results count but never shows one; DR1 only deferred its rewrite of the count; plants takes the same frame. The only count line the live animals list shows is the filtered results line when a status filter is set.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a small bold line above both lists' cards reads 'No Results', 'Showing 1 Result', 'Showing N of T Results' or 'Showing S to E of T Results' (Welsh twins on plants), worked out from the page, the size and the total, so it can disagree with the cards shown when deleted rows are dropped after the page is cut (repo-plantsfrontend-p1-057).

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list, a search that matches nothing, with no status filter set, shows an empty list with no message about it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no empty-state message on its lists outside the filtered results line, which a status filter brings up; plants takes the same frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a search with no match on either list replaces the results line with 'No notifications found' and shows no cards.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list, a tab or list holding no notifications shows no cards and no message about the empty list; on the live animals list the tab keeps its subheading and description.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no empty-state message: an empty tab shows its subheading and description only. Today's sentence also wrongly says the animals list is session-scoped. Plants' own copy quoted the same sentence, but the 9 October afternoon ruling gives plants the same frame (c-300).
requirements.deltaNote: Today a user with no notifications who is not searching sees 'You have not started any notifications in this session.' on both lists (repo-frontend-p4-068; on plants the same English sentence and the Welsh 'Nid ydych wedi dechrau unrhyw hysbysiadau yn y sesiwn hon.'), and the animals list shows 'No Results' beside it.

requirements.statement: Each notification card on the live animals list and on plants' list is labelled for screen readers 'Notification <reference>' and has the reference as its h3.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card names itself to assistive technology, and the 9 October afternoon ruling names the cards for screen readers in the reframed frame; the reference heading already exists on both lists.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each card on both lists is a GOV.UK summary card with the reference (or the notification's own id before a reference is issued) as its level-3 title, but no 'Notification <reference>' accessible name.

requirements.statement: A live animals card shows its facts in two rows: 'Commodity', 'Arrival date', 'Consignee' and 'Notification status', then the quantity, 'Origin' and 'Consignor'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card leads with what is coming, when, to whom and its status, and shows no inspection fact.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows eight facts in three rows: Commodity, Origin, 'Arrival at destination'; Consignee, Consignor, Status; 'Date created', 'Date submitted' (repo-frontend-p4-039).

requirements.statement: The card labels the arrival date 'Arrival date', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the card, and DR1's own rename row was deferred rather than judged. The 17 November ruling words the arrival date 'Arrival date at port of entry' on the question page, check your answers and the overview task list, and the 27 November ruling keeps the card's own 'Arrival date' (c-421).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Arrival at destination' on the animals card and 'Arrival' on plants' card.

requirements.statement: The card labels the status 'Notification status', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the status fact; plants takes the same card layout.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Status' on both cards.

requirements.statement: A live animals notification's card shows its quantity as 'Number of animals', from the notification's own count in the animals backend's record.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows how much is coming on every card; today no card shows a quantity, and the 9 October afternoon ruling takes the card's facts from the animals backend's record.

requirements.statement: The card shows no 'Date created' and no 'Date submitted', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card has no dates other than arrival; today's 'Date submitted' is also blank on every card, submitted ones included, on both lists.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both cards show 'Date created' and 'Date submitted', each the day the event happened in the service's own time zone; 'Date submitted' is blank in every end-to-end trace, and blank on a plants draft (repo-plantsfrontend-p1-077, trace-e2e-p3-033).

requirements.statement: The card writes the arrival date as the day, the full month name and the year, such as '21 June 2026', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card writes the arrival date with the full month name, in its code and its render alike, and nothing overrides the prototype here (c-164).
requirements.deltaNote: Today both cards write the arrival date as day, short month name and year, such as '7 Nov 2026' and '5 Mar 2026' (trace-animals-fit-p2-031, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-058); the tests repo already reads the animals card's date as 'd Month yyyy' (repo-tests-p3-073).

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list, a card whose notification has no commodity, no arrival date or no quantity yet shows 'Not applicable' for that fact.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows 'Not applicable' for a fact the notification does not hold yet, so an empty value is never mistaken for a missing card row.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a fact with no answer yet is shown with an empty value and no placeholder on both lists (repo-frontend-p4-045, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-061).

requirements.statement: The live animals card's commodity is the notification's commodity name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the commodity as the trader chose it; germinal products need the product type as well as the species (req-1738).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows the commodity's name, falling back to its commodity code and then to nothing (repo-frontend-p4-041, p4-047); a commodity chosen as Bos taurus shows 'Cow'.

requirements.statement: A draft's status is a 'Draft' tag in a colour set apart from the blue 'Submitted' tag, a submitted notification's status is a default blue GOV.UK 'Submitted' tag, and a notification being amended shows a yellow 'Amend' tag; plants' card follows the same styles for Draft, Submitted and Amend and keeps its red 'Late' tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tags every status on the list: the default GOV.UK tag for 'Submitted', a draft style for 'Draft' and yellow for 'Amend'; a notification submitted with something outstanding is shown as 'Submitted' like any other (16 November ruling, c-418). The draft colour is built from a GOV.UK tag colour modifier rather than the prototype's custom class. Plants mirrors the component (c-301).
requirements.deltaNote: Today every status on both lists is a tag: Draft blue, Submitted green, Amend yellow, Deleted grey and never shown (repo-frontend-p4-085, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-025). The completed style is req-1739.

requirements.statement: A delayed notification shows a 'Delayed' tag on an error card, with the reason for the delay as its message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows delays on the list; its own message there is placeholder copy, so the reason the record carries is shown instead.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no delay status or reason reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A notification the authorities have finished with shows the status 'Past' and is listed in the 'Past' tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 files finished notifications under 'Past' by their completed status. 'Completed' stays out as a status until a real source of completion exists (16 November ruling), so nothing reaches this tab yet. The words follow the tab vocabulary question's default (c-notification-list-003).
requirements.blockedBy: A real source of completion exists (Sam, 16 November): the authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes back to the notification record, and no completed status reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A notification chosen for inspection shows an extra 'Inspection' fact with a 'Required' tag at the end of the card's second row.
requirements.why: Not built: the Design Release 2.1 card no longer shows an 'Inspection' fact, so nothing on a card marks a notification for inspection; the inspection page that lists them is summary information, blocked with the INS dashboard.

requirements.statement: A live animals card keeps its status-driven actions, each named for screen readers with ' notification <reference>': a draft offers Resume, 'Copy as new' and Delete; a submitted notification offers View, Amend, 'Copy as new' and Delete; a notification being amended offers Resume, 'Copy as new', 'Cancel amendment' and Delete. Amend and 'Copy as new' stay link-styled buttons that post, each in its own form and in the same typeface as the links, while View, Resume, 'Cancel amendment' and Delete are links.
requirements.why: DR1 judged that the card keeps its status-driven links rather than DR1's flat 'Copy as new' and 'View', and that judgement wins over Design Release 2.1's same flat pair. Without it a trader could not resume a draft from the list. The 19 November ruling's one-form-each rule for posting buttons is what the card already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-051, p4-052 and p4-053 (proven by trace-animals-fit-p2-037, p2-042 and p2-044 and by repo-tests-p3-075 and p3-076): the card already offers these sets in this order, each posting action in its own form with the CSRF crumb and visually hidden ' notification <reference>' text.

requirements.statement: A card whose notification is delayed or completed offers a single 'View' link, opening the notification's review page.
requirements.why: DR1's judgement keeps the status-driven actions only for the cards the service builds today (draft, submitted, being amended); for the statuses the real service does not yet have, Design Release 2.1's card gives a single 'View' link (c-160).
requirements.deltaNote: Today a notification in any status other than Draft, Submitted or Amend has no actions on its card (repo-frontend-p4-054).
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; until it does, no card is in these statuses.

requirements.statement: After an action that sends the trader back to the list with that action's flag on the redirect (such as a delete), the list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert, titled 'Success', carrying that action's message; plants' deletion banner carries the same 'Success' title. Each list feature holds this wording in its own copy, and the shared notificationActions wording that other pages use stays as it is.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses one success banner titled 'Success'; the message itself is set by the action. The 9 October ruling keeps the flag on the redirect (such as ?deleted=1) rather than a message held for the trader (c-252), and the afternoon ruling gives plants' banner the same title in the same increment.

The germinal products list, its cards and its delete message copy the live animals list as it is on main today.
The germinal set's list is a copy of the reframed live animals list and depends on the animals-dashboard rows it copies.

conflicts.outcome: The 27 November ruling ranks first: the germinal products set ships its own notification list now, copying the live animals list as it is on main today, with its cards and its delete message, and does not wait for the animals dashboard theme. ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-104 is not overruled, because it still backs the germinal set's root rendering its own list whose start control starts a germinal notification; only its dependency on the animals-dashboard rows is set aside. Whether those rows later carry the germinal copy is c-notification-list-002.

conflicts.about: Whether the animals dashboard theme's rows that reframe the live animals list carry the germinal products list with them.

positions.says: The ruling leaves open how long the germinal list uses today's live animals list, and whether it moves to the reframed list.
The orchestrator's call, not Sam's words: the rows that reframe the live animals list carry the germinal list with them, so the two stay copies.
The ruling does not record whether Sam accepted that call.

conflicts.outcome: Open: the 27 November ruling ships the germinal list as a copy of today's live animals list 'for now' and does not say whether, or when, it takes the reframed list.
conflicts.question: When the animals dashboard rows reframe the live animals list, do they reframe the germinal products list in the same increments?
conflicts.default: Yes: each animals dashboard row that changes the live animals list changes the germinal products copy in the same increment, as plants' list is changed in the same increments, so the two animals lists stay copies of each other; until those rows land the germinal list is today's copy.

conflicts.about: Which words and grouping the lists' tabs, tab subheadings, status filter and finished status use: the 9 October afternoon ruling's 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed', or the 26 November prototype's 'Submitted', 'Draft and Amend' and 'Past'.

positions.says: inc-135 has 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed' tabs, as MoJ sub navigation, on the animals frontend's own list.
The list page has three tabs, 'Submitted', 'Draft and Amend' and 'Past', the first two with counts.
'Submitted' lists submitted notifications, 'Draft and Amend' drafts and notifications being amended, and 'Past' completed ones.
The category dashboard shows 'Submitted (2)', 'Draft and Amend (3)' and 'Past'.
A category dashboard has three tabs: 'Submitted (2)', 'Draft and Amend (3)' and 'Past'.

conflicts.outcome: Open: the 9 October afternoon ruling names the tabs as the prototype then had them while ruling on the component (MoJ sub navigation on the animals frontend's own list); the prototype now pinned, of 26 November, renames them, groups amendments with drafts, counts the first two and uses 'Past' for finished notifications. One reading keeps the ruling's words, the other builds the current design.
conflicts.question: Do the notification lists' tabs read 'Submitted', 'Draft and Amend' and 'Past', as the 26 November prototype has them, or 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed', as the 9 October afternoon ruling named them?
conflicts.default: The 26 November prototype's words on the live animals, germinal products and plants lists: tabs 'Submitted', 'Draft and Amend' (holding drafts and notifications being amended) and 'Past', counts on the first two, subheadings 'Submitted notifications', 'Draft notifications' and 'Past notifications' with their descriptions, the status filter's 'All statuses', 'Draft', 'Amend', 'Submitted' and 'Past', and a green 'Past' tag for a finished notification; the tabs stay MoJ sub navigation as the ruling decided.

conflicts.about: What puts a notification in the 'Past' tab: its completed status, as the prototype's code files it, or two weeks after its arrival date, as the tab's description says.

positions.says: The 'Past' tab's description says notifications move there 2 weeks after the commodity arrival date.
A notification moves to the Past tab by its completed status, not by its arrival date.
The spec proves the Past tab's copy only, not that a notification moves there 2 weeks after arrival.

conflicts.outcome: Open: the prototype says two things, and the two readings build different tabs: by status the tab stays empty until a real source of completion exists, by date it fills two weeks after each arrival.
conflicts.question: Does the 'Past' tab hold completed notifications only, or every notification two weeks after its commodity's arrival date, as its description says?
conflicts.default: Completed notifications only, as the prototype's code files them, so the tab stays empty until a real source of completion exists; the description is shown as the design words it.
